# Copper Scroll Column 2 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Copper Scroll Column 2 (treasure locations 5-8) where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 2:1 — aqueduct/water channel

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "In the aqueduct" — standard rendering of ammat ha-mayim |
| LOGOS | "In the aqueduct" — same |
| PNEUMA | "In the water channel" — descriptive |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "in the aqueduct" per EMET/LOGOS. The Hebrew ammah specifically denotes a constructed water conduit.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:5 — old washer's chamber / former washer's chamber / old laundry

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the old washer's chamber" — literal bet ha-koveset ha-yashan |
| LOGOS | "the former washer's chamber" — "former" for yashan |
| PNEUMA | "where the old laundry used to be" — dynamic paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the old washer's chamber" per EMET. PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the Hebrew structure entirely. LOGOS's "former" is acceptable but "old" is more literal for yashan.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 2:6 — terrace/level

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "on the third terrace" — literal madregah |
| LOGOS | "upon the third terrace" — formal |
| PNEUMA | "on the third level" — simplified |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "terrace" per EMET/LOGOS. Madregah specifically means a stepped terrace, not a generic level.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:10 — graves/tombs/burial sites

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "graves at its mouth" — literal qevarot |
| LOGOS | "tombs at its entrance" — formal upgrade |
| PNEUMA | "burial sites at its entrance" — expanded |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "graves at its entrance" blending EMET's "graves" (more literal for qevarot) with LOGOS's "entrance" (clearer than "mouth" for a chamber opening).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS blend.

---

## 2:11 — copy/duplicate + explanation/interpretation/key

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a copy of this document, with its explanation" |
| LOGOS | "a copy of this document, together with its interpretation" |
| PNEUMA | "a duplicate of this very scroll, with a key to reading it" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "interpretation" for pesher — this is the technical Qumran term. PNEUMA's "key to reading it" is too free. "Copy" preferred over "duplicate" as more natural.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:12 — inventory phrasing

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "an inventory of each and every thing" — literal kol echad ve-echad |
| LOGOS | "a full inventory" — compressed |
| PNEUMA | "a complete inventory of every item" — expanded |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's "an inventory of each and every thing" as it preserves the emphatic Hebrew repetition kol echad ve-echad.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 2:16-17 — vessel of incense in/made from wood type

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a vessel of incense in pine wood" — preposition be- |
| LOGOS | "an incense vessel of pine wood" — reordered |
| PNEUMA | "a vessel of incense made from pine wood" — expanded |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's word order "an incense vessel of pine wood" as more natural English while retaining precision. The preposition be- indicates the material.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements in Column 2: 7*
